learning_objective: 🎯 Marvel at the monumental stone architecture of Emperor Ashoka! Learn about giant polished pillars, the first Buddhist stupas, and life-sized Yaksha statues.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Emperor Ashoka erected massive, monolithic (single piece of stone) sandstone pillars across his empire to spread Buddhist teachings. They are famous for their brilliant, mirror-like 'Mauryan polish'.

Our National Emblem! It features four roaring lions facing four directions (symbolizing power and spreading the Dhamma), standing on a drum carved with a horse, bull, lion, and elephant, over an inverted lotus.

Stupas were solid, dome-like structures built over the relics (ashes/bones) of the Buddha. The Great Stupa at Sanchi is the most famous. It has a dome (Anda), a balcony (Harmika), a mast (Chhatra), and decorated gateways (Toranas).

Large, life-size stone statues of folk deities were made. The most famous is the 'Didarganj Yakshi' holding a chauri (fly-whisk). She represents the ideal of physical beauty and has the signature Mauryan high polish.

The Mauryans started the tradition of carving caves out of solid rock mountains for monks to meditate in. The Lomas Rishi Cave in the Barabar Hills has a beautifully carved, arched entrance resembling wooden architecture.

fun_activity.title: 🪙 Coin Decoding
fun_activity.instructions: Take a 1 Rupee or 5 Rupee coin and a magnifying glass. Look at the Lion Capital emblem. You only see 3 lions (the 4th is hidden behind). Below them, find the 'Dharmachakra' (wheel) in the center, flanked by a horse on the left and a bull on the right!

exam_tips: 📌 Drawing and labeling the parts of the Sarnath Lion Capital (Lions, Abacus/Drum, Chakra, Inverted Lotus) is a high-value question.
📌 Be able to label the architectural parts of a Stupa (Anda, Harmika, Chhatra, Pradakshina Path, Torana).
📌 Mention 'Mauryan Polish' whenever discussing any sculpture from this period; it is the defining characteristic of 3rd Century BCE art.
quick_recap: ⭐ Mauryan pillars were carved from a single piece of Chunar sandstone.
⭐ The Sarnath Lion Capital commemorates the Buddha's 'First Sermon' (Dharmachakrapravartana).
⭐ Stupas originally started as burial mounds but became objects of deep veneration in Buddhism.
